# Model and source

Sahasrabudhe 2026 reports three Phase 1 studies of oral ceftibuten given with
avibactam tomilopil, an oral prodrug of the beta-lactamase inhibitor
avibactam, and a joint population PK model of plasma cis-ceftibuten and
avibactam fitted to all three. The paper gives two versions of the joint
model, and both are packaged:

* `Sahasrabudhe_2026_ceftibuten_avibactam`, the **final model**
  (Supplemental Table S12).
* `Sahasrabudhe_2026_ceftibuten_avibactam_crcl`, the **simulation model**
  (Supplemental Table S15). The authors used it for the joint probability of
  target attainment (jPTA) simulations that selected the Phase 3 regimen. It
  replaces the power effect of BSA-normalised creatinine clearance with a
  linear effect of absolute creatinine clearance (slopes fixed from published
  renal-impairment studies) and drops several covariates (Table S13).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sahasrabudhe_2026_ceftibuten_avibactam"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70263> (open access, with Supplemental Appendix)

Both models share one structure. Ceftibuten (the unsuffixed parent) has a
depot, five transit compartments and one disposition compartment. Avibactam
(suffix `_avi`) has a depot, three transit compartments and two disposition
compartments. Within each drug every transit step uses the same rate
constant `ktr`. Avibactam tomilopil doses go into `depot_avi` in **mg of
prodrug**. The model multiplies them by the molecular-weight ratio 0.674 to
give avibactam equivalents (see Assumptions). Both models return total plasma
concentrations in mg/L: `Cc` for cis-ceftibuten and `Cc_avi` for avibactam.

# Population

The analysis set was 71 healthy adults (57 men, 14 women) from three
single-centre studies in Australia and Belgium (Table 1, Table 2):

* **C4691002**: single ascending doses of avibactam tomilopil oral suspension
  (300, 900, 1350 mg), fed with a regular meal, given alone.
* **C4691001**: Part 1 gave single doses of ceftibuten 400-1600 mg with or
  without avibactam tomilopil 900-1350 mg as separate capsules (regular meal).
  Part 2 gave ceftibuten 400 or 800 mg with avibactam tomilopil 900 or 1350 mg
  every 8 h for 7 days, fed, except Day 7, which was fasted.
* **C4691003**: single doses comparing separate capsules (ceftibuten 400 mg +
  avibactam tomilopil 1125 mg, fasted) with a fixed-dose tablet (ceftibuten
  402 mg + avibactam tomilopil 1200 mg) fasted and after a high-fat meal.

Median age 32 years (range 18-59), median body weight 76.6 kg (50.1-101),
median creatinine clearance 124 mL/min (58.5-179) and median BSA-normalised
creatinine clearance 109 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (68.3-160). The cohort was 62% White,
22.5% Asian, 5.6% Black and 7% other race (2.8% not reported). There were 1467
cis-ceftibuten and 1707 avibactam plasma observations.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Sahasrabudhe_2026_ceftibuten_avibactam")()$population[c("n_subjects", "n_studies", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct")])
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value also carries an in-file comment that names its table row.

| Equation / parameter | Final model (Table S12) | Simulation model (Table S15) |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (ceftibuten CL/F, L/h) | log(4.24) | log(4.4) |
| `lvc` (ceftibuten Vc/F, L) | log(17.9) | log(19.4) |
| `lktr` (ceftibuten ktr, 1/h) | log(2.55) | log(3.02) |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.272, power on nCrCL/112 | 0.00794 per mL/min, linear on CrCL - 112, fixed |
| `e_fasted_ktr` | 1.62 | 0.65 |
| `e_fasted_fdepot` | -0.187 | removed |
| `e_mono_fdepot` (ceftibuten alone) | 0.343 | removed |
| `e_dose_fdepot` | -0.211, power on dose/400 | -0.126, step for dose > 800 mg |
| `e_highfat_ktr` | 1.02 | removed |
| `e_highfat_fdepot` | -0.255 | removed |
| `lcl_avi` (avibactam CL/F, L/h) | log(21.1) | log(20.8) |
| `lvc_avi` (avibactam Vc/F, L) | log(73.2) | log(76.6) |
| `lq_avi` (avibactam Q/F, L/h) | log(0.34) | log(0.356) |
| `lvp_avi` (avibactam Vp/F, L) | log(12.1) | log(12.4) |
| `lktr_avi` (avibactam ktr, 1/h) | log(1.65) | log(1.83) |
| `e_crcl_cl_avi` | 0.316, power on nCrCL/112 | 0.00931 per mL/min, linear, fixed |
| `e_fasted_ktr_avi` | 2.32 | 1.51 |
| `e_fasted_fdepot_avi` | -0.556 | -0.523 |
| `e_susp_ktr_avi` | 2.37 | 2.02 |
| `e_susp_fdepot_avi` | 0.384 | 0.317 |
| `e_mono_cl_avi` (avibactam tomilopil alone) | 0.272 | 0.237 |
| `e_dose_fdepot_avi` | 0.184, power on dose/1350 | removed |
| `e_highfat_ktr_avi` | 0.555 | removed |
| `e_highfat_fdepot_avi` | not in model | 0.192 |
| `e_fasted_cl_avi` | -0.423 | -0.439 |
| `e_wt_cl_q`, `e_wt_vc_vp` | 0.75, 1 (fixed), WT/70 | same |
| IIV CL, Vc of both drugs (4 x 4 block) | 19.7, 21.8, 19.2, 29.3 %CV + 6 covariances | 27, 27.4, 21.5, 26.2 %CV + 6 covariances |
| IIV ktr (ceftibuten, avibactam) | 34.7, 38 %CV | 41.8, 37.8 %CV |
| `expSd`, `expSd_avi` (log-scale residual SD) | 0.463, 0.42 | 0.484, 0.422 |
| Transit chains (5 for ceftibuten, 3 for avibactam) | Results, 'Final Population Pharmacokinetic Model' | same |
| Allometry, nCrCL and dose forms | Methods; Table S12 footnote | Table S15 footnote |
| Covariate shift form `1 + theta x indicator` | Figure S4 (top) forest-plot ratios | Figure S4 (bottom) |
| Prodrug-to-avibactam mass ratio 0.674 | back-calculated from Table S11 | same |

All covariate shifts are relative to the reference condition: both drugs
given together as capsules or tablet with a regular meal (Table S12
footnote). `fasted` is `1 - FED`. "Ceftibuten alone" is
`1 - CONMED_AVIBACTAMTOMILOPIL` and "avibactam tomilopil alone" is
`1 - CONMED_CEFTIBUTEN`. The forest plots in Figure S4 fix the functional
forms. For example, the final model's ceftibuten "single agent" ratio of 1.34
equals 1 + 0.343, its "CTB 200 mg" ratio of 1.16 equals (200/400)^-0.211, and
the simulation model's CrCL 150 / 60 mL/min ratios of 1.30 / 0.59 for
ceftibuten equal 1 + 0.00794 x (150 - 112) and 1 + 0.00794 x (60 - 112).

# Virtual cohort and helpers

Body weight and BSA-normalised creatinine clearance are drawn from normal
distributions with the analysis-set means and SDs of Table 2, truncated to
the observed ranges. Each Phase 1 arm has 100 virtual subjects.

```{r helpers}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260901)
set.seed(20260901)

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- stats::rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- stats::rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}

# One arm: per-subject covariates, ceftibuten doses into depot, avibactam
# tomilopil (mg prodrug) into depot_avi, observations on the ceftibuten
# central state. The model declares two endpoints (Cc, Cc_avi), so
# observation rows carry dvid = 1 alongside the ODE-state cmt; rxode2 then
# returns both endpoint columns on every observation row.
make_arm <- function(n, arm_id, ctb, avp, fed = 1, highfat = 0, susp = 0,
                     n_dose = 1, tau = 8, obs_times, crcl = NULL, wt = NULL,
                     id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  cov <- tibble(
    id = ids,
    arm_id = arm_id,
    WT = if (is.null(wt)) rtrunc_norm(n, 76.4, 12.5, 50.1, 101) else wt,
    CRCL = if (is.null(crcl)) rtrunc_norm(n, 111, 17.3, 68.3, 160) else crcl,
    FED = fed,
    FED_HIGHFAT = highfat,
    FORM_AVIBACTAMTOMILOPIL_SUSP = susp,
    CONMED_CEFTIBUTEN = as.integer(ctb > 0),
    CONMED_AVIBACTAMTOMILOPIL = as.integer(avp > 0),
    # A drug that is not given still needs a finite dose covariate for its
    # bioavailability expression; the nominal reference dose is used.
    DOSE_CEFTIBUTEN_MG = if (ctb > 0) ctb else 400,
    DOSE_AVIBACTAMTOMILOPIL_MG = if (avp > 0) avp else 1350
  )
  dose_t <- (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau
  doses <- bind_rows(
    if (ctb > 0) tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_t) |> mutate(amt = ctb, cmt = "depot"),
    if (avp > 0) tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_t) |> mutate(amt = avp, cmt = "depot_avi")
  ) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central", evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

mod_final <- readModelDb("Sahasrabudhe_2026_ceftibuten_avibactam")
mod_sim <- readModelDb("Sahasrabudhe_2026_ceftibuten_avibactam_crcl")
```

# Single-dose Phase 1 arms (final model)

```{r single-dose-arms}
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm_id, ~arm, ~ctb, ~avp, ~fed, ~highfat, ~susp,
  1L, "C4691002 AVP 300 mg susp", 0, 300, 1, 0, 1,
  2L, "C4691002 AVP 900 mg susp", 0, 900, 1, 0, 1,
  3L, "C4691002 AVP 1350 mg susp", 0, 1350, 1, 0, 1,
  4L, "C4691001 CTB 400 + AVP 900", 400, 900, 1, 0, 0,
  5L, "C4691001 CTB 800 + AVP 1350", 800, 1350, 1, 0, 0,
  6L, "C4691001 CTB 800 alone", 800, 0, 1, 0, 0,
  7L, "C4691001 CTB 1200 + AVP 1350", 1200, 1350, 1, 0, 0,
  8L, "C4691001 CTB 1600 alone", 1600, 0, 1, 0, 0,
  9L, "C4691003 capsule fasted", 400, 1125, 0, 0, 0,
  10L, "C4691003 tablet fasted", 402, 1200, 0, 0, 0,
  11L, "C4691003 tablet high-fat fed", 402, 1200, 1, 1, 0
)

obs_sd <- c(seq(0, 8, by = 0.25), seq(9, 24, by = 1), seq(26, 48, by = 2))
n_per_arm <- 100L
ev_sd <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  make_arm(n_per_arm, a$arm_id, a$ctb, a$avp, a$fed, a$highfat, a$susp,
           obs_times = obs_sd, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_sd[ev_sd$evid == 1, c("id", "time", "cmt")]))

sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_final, events = ev_sd, keep = "arm_id") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, time, arm_id, Cc, Cc_avi) |>
  left_join(arms |> select(arm_id, arm, ctb, avp), by = "arm_id")
```

## Figure 1: median concentration-time profiles

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates the layout of Figure 1 of Sahasrabudhe 2026 (median plasma
# avibactam, panels a, b, d; median cis-ceftibuten, panels e, g).
prof <- bind_rows(
  sim_sd |> filter(avp > 0) |> transmute(arm, time, analyte = "Avibactam", conc = Cc_avi),
  sim_sd |> filter(ctb > 0) |> transmute(arm, time, analyte = "cis-Ceftibuten", conc = Cc)
) |>
  filter(time <= 24) |>
  group_by(analyte, arm, time) |>
  summarise(median = median(conc), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(prof, aes(time, median, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Median plasma concentration (mg/L)",
       colour = NULL,
       caption = "Simulated with the final model; compare with Figure 1 of Sahasrabudhe 2026.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

## PKNCA and comparison with Tables 3 and 4

```{r pknca-single}
run_nca <- function(conc_df, dose_df) {
  conc_df <- bind_rows(
    conc_df,
    conc_df |> distinct(id, arm) |> mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)
  ) |>
    distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, arm, time)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | arm + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                          aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}

dose_rows <- ev_sd |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  left_join(arms |> select(arm_id, arm), by = "arm_id")

nca_ctb <- run_nca(
  sim_sd |> filter(ctb > 0, !is.na(Cc)) |> transmute(id, arm, time, conc = Cc),
  dose_rows |> filter(cmt == "depot") |> select(id, arm, time, amt)
)
nca_avi <- run_nca(
  sim_sd |> filter(avp > 0, !is.na(Cc_avi)) |> transmute(id, arm, time, conc = Cc_avi),
  dose_rows |> filter(cmt == "depot_avi") |> select(id, arm, time, amt)
)
```

Published values are geometric means, except median Tmax and arithmetic-mean
half-life. They are converted from ng/mL to mg/L. `ncaComparisonTable()`
summarises the simulated cohort by its median.

```{r nca-compare-ctb}
pub_ctb <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "C4691001 CTB 400 + AVP 900", 18.17, 3.21, 94.73, 3.073,
  "C4691001 CTB 800 + AVP 1350", 25.47, 4.03, 155.8, 2.708,
  "C4691001 CTB 800 alone", 30.51, 3.50, 173.2, 2.908,
  "C4691001 CTB 1200 + AVP 1350", 27.12, 5.05, 184.9, 3.138,
  "C4691001 CTB 1600 alone", 44.99, 4.01, 321.9, 3.180,
  "C4691003 capsule fasted", 15.37, 2.54, 77.02, 2.783,
  "C4691003 tablet fasted", 13.12, 2.50, 73.64, 2.780,
  "C4691003 tablet high-fat fed", 12.44, 3.00, 76.30, 2.903
)
cmp_ctb <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_ctb, reference = pub_ctb, by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_ctb, caption = "cis-Ceftibuten: simulated (final model) vs Table 4. * differs by >20%.")
```

cmp_avi <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_avi, reference = pub_avi, by = "arm",
  params = c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_avi, caption = "Avibactam: simulated (final model) vs Table 3. * differs by >20%.")

# Disposition half-lives of the typical (70 kg, nCrCL 112) avibactam
# two-compartment system, fed, with ceftibuten.
k10 <- 21.1 / 73.2
k12 <- 0.34 / 73.2
k21 <- 0.34 / 12.1
ab <- k10 + k12 + k21
lambda <- (ab + c(1, -1) * sqrt(ab^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
avi_half_lives <- log(2) / lambda
avi_half_lives

```

```{r nca-checks}
auc_pct <- function(nca, pub) {
  as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
    group_by(arm) |>
    summarise(sim = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    inner_join(pub |> select(arm, ref = aucinf.obs), by = "arm") |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * (sim - ref) / ref)
}
auc_ctb <- auc_pct(nca_ctb, pub_ctb)
auc_avi <- auc_pct(nca_avi, pub_avi)
knitr::kable(bind_rows(auc_ctb |> mutate(analyte = "cis-ceftibuten"),
                       auc_avi |> mutate(analyte = "avibactam")) |>
               mutate(across(c(sim, ref, pct), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
               rename("Analyte" = analyte, "Arm" = arm, "Simulated median AUCinf (mg*h/L)" = sim,
                      "Published geometric mean (mg*h/L)" = ref, "% difference" = pct),
             caption = "AUCinf across all single-dose arms.")

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed clearance, dose scaling or molecular-weight
  # ratio moves every arm by tens of percent.
  abs(median(auc_ctb$pct)) < 15,
  abs(median(auc_avi$pct)) < 15,
  # Envelope: the cohort medians of every arm stay within 35% of the
  # published geometric means.
  all(abs(auc_ctb$pct) < 35),
  all(abs(auc_avi$pct) < 35)
)
```

The final model tracks the published exposures in most arms. The visible
misses are structural, not a transcription problem:

* **Ceftibuten 1200 and 1600 mg.** The power dose effect on bioavailability
  (exponent -0.211) does not fully capture how sharply exposure flattens
  above 800 mg (Results: "less than dose proportional for ceftibuten doses of
  800 mg and higher"). The simulation model later replaced it with a step
  above 800 mg.
* **Avibactam after a high-fat meal (tablet fed).** The final model has no
  high-fat-meal effect on avibactam bioavailability, because the joint fit
  dropped it (Table S1, step S5). So the high-fat arm is predicted from the
  regular-meal reference and under-predicts the observed 49 mg*h/L. The
  simulation model adds the effect back (+19.2%).
* **Avibactam terminal half-life.** The published peripheral compartment is
  small and slowly exchanging (Q/F 0.34 L/h, Vp/F 12.1 L). The typical
  avibactam profile therefore has a dominant phase with a half-life of
  `r signif(avi_half_lives[1], 2)` h and a low-amplitude slow phase with a
  half-life of `r signif(avi_half_lives[2], 2)` h. Over a 48-h simulated
  profile, PKNCA fits the slow phase and returns terminal half-lives of
  about 12-25 h. The published NCA half-lives (1.5-5.7 h, from sampling
  windows of 12-72 h) describe the dominant phase. The comparison is
  therefore not like-for-like, and avibactam half-life is left out of the
  table.
* **Time to peak.** The simulated median Tmax is earlier than observed in
  the fasted and suspension arms (1.25-1.5 h vs 1.8-3 h). These arms carry
  the large fasted and suspension multipliers on `ktr` (x 3.3 to x 3.4 for
  avibactam, x 2.6 for ceftibuten fasted). Exposure (AUC) in the same arms
  matches within 20%.

## Multiple dosing, Day 6 (fed)

Study C4691001 Part 2 cohorts 1-3 received doses every 8 h. Day 6 starts at
120 h, which is the 16th dose. The comparison uses Tables S8 and S10.

```{r multiple-dose}
md_arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm_id, ~arm, ~ctb, ~avp,
  21L, "CTB 400 + AVP 1350 q8h", 400, 1350,
  22L, "CTB 800 + AVP 1350 q8h", 800, 1350,
  23L, "CTB 400 + AVP 900 q8h", 400, 900
)
obs_md <- seq(120, 128, by = 0.25)
ev_md <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(md_arms)), function(i) {
  a <- md_arms[i, ]
  make_arm(n_per_arm, a$arm_id, a$ctb, a$avp, n_dose = 16, tau = 8,
           obs_times = obs_md, id_offset = 5000L + (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
sim_md <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_final, events = ev_md, keep = "arm_id") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, time, arm_id, Cc, Cc_avi) |>
  left_join(md_arms |> select(arm_id, arm), by = "arm_id")

md_dose <- ev_md |> filter(evid == 1) |> left_join(md_arms |> select(arm_id, arm), by = "arm_id")
nca_ss <- function(conc_df, dose_df) {
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | arm + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 120, end = 128, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_md_ctb <- nca_ss(sim_md |> transmute(id, arm, time, conc = Cc),
                     md_dose |> filter(cmt == "depot") |> select(id, arm, time, amt))
nca_md_avi <- nca_ss(sim_md |> transmute(id, arm, time, conc = Cc_avi),
                     md_dose |> filter(cmt == "depot_avi") |> select(id, arm, time, amt))

pub_md_ctb <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "CTB 400 + AVP 1350 q8h", 22.63, 104.2,
  "CTB 800 + AVP 1350 q8h", 45.64, 224.3,
  "CTB 400 + AVP 900 q8h", 20.68, 93.59
)
pub_md_avi <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "CTB 400 + AVP 1350 q8h", 7.940, 39.57,
  "CTB 800 + AVP 1350 q8h", 8.676, 45.13,
  "CTB 400 + AVP 900 q8h", 6.159, 29.92
)
knitr::kable(nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_md_ctb, reference = pub_md_ctb, by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"), tolerance_pct = 20
), caption = "cis-Ceftibuten Day 6 (AUC over the 120-128 h interval) vs Table S10. * differs by >20%.")
knitr::kable(nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_md_avi, reference = pub_md_avi, by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"), tolerance_pct = 20
), caption = "Avibactam Day 6 (AUC over the 120-128 h interval) vs Table S8. * differs by >20%.")
```

Avibactam steady-state exposure matches Table S8 within 20% for AUC. The
simulated ceftibuten Day 6 exposure is lower than observed, most of all for
800 mg q8h. The observed ceftibuten accumulation ratios on Day 6 (1.38-1.98,
Table S10) are larger than a 3-h half-life with 8-h dosing allows (about
1.1). The paper notes that the regular-meal effect in C4691001 could not be
resolved "owing to confounding from accumulation". The final model was
fitted to these data as published, and no parameter is adjusted here.

# Simulation model: renal function and jPTA

## Clearance across creatinine clearance

```{r crcl-cl}
crcl_grid <- c(15, 30, 50, 80, 112, 150)
typ_sim <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_sim)
# One single-subject solve per CrCL value: a typical-value (zero-omega)
# solve of several subjects at once makes rxode2 warn.
sim_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(crcl_grid), function(i) {
  ev <- make_arm(1L, i, 400, 1200, obs_times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.1),
                 crcl = crcl_grid[i], wt = 70)
  rxode2::rxSolve(typ_sim, events = ev) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(arm_id = i)
}))
auc_trap <- function(t, c) sum(diff(t) * (head(c, -1) + tail(c, -1)) / 2)
cl_tab <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(arm_id) |>
  summarise(auc24_ctb = auc_trap(time, Cc), auc24_avi = auc_trap(time, Cc_avi), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(CrCL = crcl_grid[arm_id],
         cl_ctb = 4.4 * (1 + 0.00794 * (CrCL - 112)),
         cl_avi = 20.8 * (1 + 0.00931 * (CrCL - 112)))
knitr::kable(cl_tab |> select(CrCL, cl_ctb, cl_avi, auc24_ctb, auc24_avi) |>
               mutate(across(-CrCL, \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
               rename("CrCL (mL/min)" = CrCL, "Ceftibuten CL/F (L/h)" = cl_ctb,
                      "Avibactam CL/F (L/h)" = cl_avi,
                      "Ceftibuten AUC0-24, single dose (mg*h/L)" = auc24_ctb,
                      "Avibactam AUC0-24, single dose (mg*h/L)" = auc24_avi),
             caption = "Typical 70 kg patient, single ceftibuten 400 mg + avibactam tomilopil 1200 mg, fed.")
```

The linear CrCL term makes avibactam CL/F fall toward zero as CrCL
approaches about 4.6 mL/min. Below that it would turn negative. The model is
therefore not meant for end-stage renal disease.

## Figure 2 / Table S16: joint probability of target attainment

The authors drew covariates for 1000 virtual patients with complicated
urinary tract infection from an earlier aztreonam-avibactam population PK
data set that is not published. Here, as an assumed stand-in, each regimen
has 200 virtual patients. Body weight is normal (mean 75 kg, SD 15,
truncated to 45-130 kg). Creatinine clearance is log-normal (median
80 mL/min, CV 45%, truncated to 15-200 mL/min). Each patient receives
ceftibuten 400 mg + avibactam tomilopil q8h, fed, for 10 days. On Day 10:

free cis-ceftibuten (unbound fraction 0.61) must exceed the MIC for a set
fraction of the day, and free avibactam (unbound fraction 0.92) must reach a
set AUC0-24. The Methods give target ranges ("50% to >99% fT > MIC" and
"50-100 ug h/mL fAUC0-24,ss") but not the pair used for Table S16. Two pairs
bracket that range:

* **lower**: fT>MIC >= 50% and fAUC0-24 >= 50 mg*h/L;
* **upper**: fT>MIC > 99% and fAUC0-24 >= 100 mg*h/L.

Because the cohort and the exact targets are assumptions, the table is
illustrative, not a reproduction of Table S16.

```{r jpta}
n_pta <- 200L
make_pta <- function(avp, arm_id, id_offset) {
  wt <- rtrunc_norm(n_pta, 75, 15, 45, 130)
  crcl <- pmin(pmax(exp(stats::rnorm(n_pta, log(80), 0.43)), 15), 200)
  make_arm(n_pta, arm_id, 400, avp, n_dose = 30, tau = 8,
           obs_times = seq(216, 240, by = 0.1), crcl = crcl, wt = wt,
           id_offset = id_offset)
}
pta_arms <- tibble(arm_id = 31:32, avp = c(800, 1200))
ev_pta <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pta_arms)), function(i) {
  make_pta(pta_arms$avp[i], pta_arms$arm_id[i], 10000L + (i - 1L) * n_pta)
}))
sim_pta <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sim, events = ev_pta, keep = "arm_id") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, time, arm_id, Cc, Cc_avi)

mics <- c(0.12, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)
pta_subj <- sim_pta |>
  group_by(arm_id, id) |>
  summarise(fauc_avi = auc_trap(time, 0.92 * Cc_avi),
            fctb = list(0.61 * Cc), .groups = "drop")
pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(pta_subj, MIC = mics) |>
  mutate(ft_mic = vapply(seq_along(fctb), function(i) mean(fctb[[i]] > MIC[i]), numeric(1)),
         joint_lower = ft_mic >= 0.5 & fauc_avi >= 50,
         joint_upper = ft_mic > 0.99 & fauc_avi >= 100) |>
  group_by(arm_id, MIC) |>
  summarise(jpta_lower = 100 * mean(joint_lower),
            jpta_upper = 100 * mean(joint_upper), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(pta_arms, by = "arm_id") |>
  mutate(regimen = paste0("CTB 400 mg + AVP ", avp, " mg q8h"))

table_s16 <- tibble(
  MIC = rep(mics, 2),
  avp = rep(c(800, 1200), each = 6),
  published = c(95.0, 95.0, 95.0, 95.0, 91.8, 67.6, 99.6, 99.6, 99.5, 99.2, 93.3, 67.6)
)
knitr::kable(pta |> left_join(table_s16, by = c("MIC", "avp")) |>
               select(regimen, MIC, jpta_lower, jpta_upper, published) |>
               mutate(across(c(jpta_lower, jpta_upper), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
               rename("Regimen" = regimen, "MIC (mg/L)" = MIC,
                      "Simulated jPTA, lower targets (%)" = jpta_lower,
                      "Simulated jPTA, upper targets (%)" = jpta_upper,
                      "Table S16, fed (%)" = published),
             caption = "jPTA from the simulation model under an assumed cUTI covariate distribution.")

pta |>
  pivot_longer(c(jpta_lower, jpta_upper), names_to = "targets", values_to = "jpta",
               names_prefix = "jpta_") |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(MIC), jpta, colour = regimen, linetype = targets,
             group = interaction(regimen, targets))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Ceftibuten MIC (mg/L)", y = "jPTA (%)", colour = NULL, linetype = "Targets",
       caption = "Compare with Figure 2 of Sahasrabudhe 2026 (fed, ceftibuten 400 mg + avibactam tomilopil 1200 mg q8h).") +
  theme_bw()
```

With the lower targets, the jPTA plateau at low MIC (about 92% for
800 mg and 97-98% for 1200 mg avibactam tomilopil in the cohort rendered
here) is close to the published 95% and 99.6%. It stays above 90% at 4 mg/L,
however, where Table S16 drops to 67.6%. With the upper targets, the
avibactam fAUC0-24 >= 100 mg*h/L requirement caps jPTA (about 50% and 75%)
at every MIC, and the ceftibuten target matters only at 4 mg/L. Neither
bracket reproduces both the high plateau and the steep drop at 4 mg/L.
That pattern fits the low avibactam target combined with a stricter
ceftibuten time-above-MIC target, but the paper does not state the pair, and
its cUTI covariate set is not available either. The higher avibactam
tomilopil dose raises jPTA through the avibactam exposure target, as in
Table S16.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two models.** The final model (Table S12) and the simulation model
  (Table S15) are packaged as separate files. The paper reports the
  simulation model as the primary basis for dose selection, not as a
  sensitivity analysis.
* **Prodrug dose conversion.** The paper scales "avibactam tomilopil dose
  ... to the equivalent avibactam dose, using molecular weight fraction" but
  does not print the fraction. The maintainers back-calculated it from Table
  S11, whose fraction-excreted column divides the amount excreted by the
  avibactam-equivalent dose: 92.0 mg / 0.455 / 300 mg = 0.674, 273.5 / 0.451
  / 900 = 0.674 and 510.8 / 0.561 / 1350 = 0.674. The hydroxypivalic-acid
  columns give a consistent, separate ratio (7.2 mg / 0.080 / 300 mg =
  0.30 for every dose). The model applies 0.674 in `f(depot_avi)`. Doses are
  entered in mg of prodrug, and the `DOSE_AVIBACTAMTOMILOPIL_MG` covariate is
  also prodrug mass, matching the paper's reference dose of 1350 mg.
* **Transit chain.** "A depot compartment and five transit compartments
  linked with a Ktr" (three for avibactam) is coded as depot -> transit1 ...
  transitN -> central, with every step at the single estimated `ktr`. No
  separate absorption rate constant is reported.
* **IIV scale.** Table S12 and Table S15 print the IIV diagonals as CV%. They
  are taken as sqrt(omega^2) x 100, so omega^2 = (CV/100)^2, with the printed
  covariances used as they are. With this reading the Table S15 covariances
  reproduce the correlations printed in Table S14 (for example 0.0582 /
  (0.270 x 0.274) = 0.787 against 0.788). Residual CV% values are taken as
  log-scale SDs in the same way (0.123 / (0.484 x 0.422) = 0.60 against the
  printed residual correlation of 0.601).
* **Correlated residual error omitted.** NONMEM estimated a covariance
  between the cis-ceftibuten and avibactam log-residuals (0.117 in the final
  model, 0.123 in the simulation model). nlmixr2 residual-error models cannot
  correlate two endpoints, so each endpoint keeps its own `lnorm()` SD. This
  affects only the joint spread of simulated observations, not individual
  predictions.
* **Linear CrCL form.** The Table S15 footnote writes the effect as
  "(CrCL-112)*theta". It is coded as `CL x (1 + theta x (CrCL - 112))`, the form
  that reproduces the Figure S4 (bottom) ratios. CrCL here is absolute
  Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance in mL/min. The final model instead
  uses BSA-normalised CrCL in mL/min/1.73 m^2. Both models centre at
  112 mL/min, as printed, although Table 2 gives medians of 124 (absolute) and
  109 (normalised).
* **Unused-drug covariates.** For an arm that does not give one of the drugs,
  that drug's dose covariate is set to its reference dose (400 mg ceftibuten,
  1350 mg avibactam tomilopil). This keeps the bioavailability expression
  finite and has no effect because no amount enters that depot.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Phase 1 covariates are normal draws matching the
  Table 2 means and SDs. The jPTA cohort is an assumption (see above),
  because the cUTI covariate set the authors used is not published.
* **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-11-17.
